title: backlog.py set takes --commit, so the orchestrator rewords an item on a worker's branch without resuming its session
goal: SP-rsmmwzr2 close: ST-unrlktke's researched check failed only on its goal's wording; set has no --commit, so the orchestrator resumed the Sonnet worker to run set and commit the item file, which cost about 2.6 USD for a two-line change (result.json of the resume). backlog.py --root <worktree> set ID ... --commit commits the item file alone with KB-Work, as answer --commit does.

run:
import subprocess,sys
p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/backlog.py','set','--help'],capture_output=True,text=True)
ok=p.returncode==0 and '--commit' in p.stdout
print('set --help exits 0 and names --commit:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
